sources.entry: WizardLM - WizardLM is a family of fine-tuned models based on open-source language models, optimized for instruction-following tasks. Known for its high-quality performance in natural language understanding and generation, WizardLM can be run on local servers.

summary.one_liner: WizardLM is the official repository for a family of instruction-following open LLMs (WizardLM, WizardCoder, WizardMath) trained with the Evol-Instruct method to handle complex instructions.
summary.what_it_does: The README is the project page for a family of LLMs fine-tuned to follow complex instructions: WizardLM (general chat, based on Llama models), WizardCoder (code generation), and WizardMath (math reasoning). It describes the Evol-Instruct method, which uses an LLM to automatically generate instructions of varying difficulty and skill range. It lists benchmark results on HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, GSM8K, MATH, MT-Bench, AlpacaEval, MMLU, ARC, TruthfulQA and HellaSwag, comparing against GPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5, Gemini Pro and other models. Model checkpoints are linked on Hugging Face in tables by version and size (from 1B to 70B). The README also gives the prompt templates to use for each model family and points to src/infer_wizardlm13b.py for inference, plus an Evol Script for running Evol-Instruct. It contains citations for the WizardLM, WizardCoder and WizardMath papers.
use_cases: generate code from natural language prompts
solve grade-school and competition math word problems
generate synthetic instruction datasets with Evol-Instruct
research on instruction tuning of LLMs
how_to_run: Download model weights from the Hugging Face links in the README tables
Use the prompt format given in the README for the chosen model (Vicuna-style for WizardLM, Alpaca-style for WizardCoder and WizardMath)
Run inference using src/infer_wizardlm13b.py as referenced in the README
Use the Evol Script provided in the repository to generate evolved instructions
notable: Evol-Instruct method that uses an LLM to automatically create instructions of varying difficulty
Covers three model families: general chat (WizardLM), code (WizardCoder), and math (WizardMath)
WizardCoder-33B-V1.1 reports SOTA open-source code results on the EvalPlus leaderboard per the README
Each model family uses a specific prompt template that the README says must be followed to match its demo
caveats: Restricted to academic research use only per the disclaimer; commercial use is not permitted
README says the training data release is delayed pending legal review, and researchers cannot publicly release it without authorization
Output accuracy is not guaranteed by the project, and the project accepts no liability for model outputs
Several older models (e.g. WizardLM-13B-V1.1, 30B, 13B-V1.0, 7B) are listed as non-commercial and some use the Llama 2 license instead
summary.license: Mixed per model: Llama 2 License for some models and non-commercial terms for others; the README's overall disclaimer restricts use to academic research
